issues.legal_issue: A person exposed to recovery of public dues is entitled to a hearing before the responsible official determines the sum due and issues a recovery certificate.
material_facts: A company borrowed money from a financial corporation and defaulted; after the company was wound up and its assets were sold, an unpaid balance remained.

The financial corporation sought to recover the balance through a statutory process requiring its Managing Director to determine the sum due before sending a certificate to the Collector for recovery as land revenue.
The appellant, who had been a director of the company when some loans were taken, was included among the persons from whom recovery was sought.
The Managing Director determined the amount and sent a recovery certificate without giving the appellant notice or an opportunity to be heard.
issues.conclusion: The Managing Director’s determination and the consequent recovery certificate were vitiated because the appellant had not been heard. The Court set them aside, along with the High Court judgment, while permitting fresh recovery proceedings in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(1)(b) of the Haryana Public Moneys (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1979, the Managing Director must determine the sum due; Sections 3(2) and 3(3) make the resulting certificate the basis for recovery as arrears of land revenue, and Section 3(4) excludes civil-court jurisdiction over recovery proceedings. Because the determination has civil consequences, is final and conclusive in effect, and replaces adjudication by a civil court, natural justice requires notice and a hearing before the determination. Director of Industries, U.P. v. Deep Chand Aggarwal, 1980 (2) SCR 1015, upheld a different statute’s validity but did not decide whether natural justice required a hearing; the U.P. provision lacked a requirement equivalent to Section 3(1)(b), and the Court expressed no opinion on statutes lacking such a requirement.

predicates.public_dues_certificate_recovery: A proceeding was brought to recover public dues through a statutory certificate and revenue-recovery process.
predicates.responsible_official_must_determine_amou: The governing recovery process required a designated official to determine the amount due before a certificate could be sent for recovery.
predicates.affected_person_not_heard_before_determi: The person against whom recovery was sought received no notice or opportunity to be heard before the designated official determined the amount.

issues.definition: When a statutory public-dues recovery proceeding requires an official to determine the amount due, the determination and resulting recovery certificate are invalid if the affected person was not heard beforehand.
